registers.name: CLKCTRL

fields.name: WRTLOCK
fields.text: Writing it locks the generic clock chosen by CLKCTRL.ID, the generator chosen by CLKCTRL.GEN and that generator's division factor against further writes, until a power reset. Generator 0 cannot be locked.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Picks the generic clock that the CLKCTRL write sets up. A power reset clears CLKCTRL for every ID, RTC included; a user reset clears it for one ID only when that ID's WRTLOCK is 0 and the ID is not the RTC. After a power reset: RTC has GEN 0x00, CLKEN 0, WRTLOCK 0; WDT has GEN 0x02, CLKEN equal to the WDT Enable bit of the NVM User Row and WRTLOCK equal to its WDT Always-On bit; every other ID has GEN 0x00, CLKEN 0, WRTLOCK 0. After a user reset: RTC's GEN and CLKEN go to 0x00 when WRTLOCK=0 and CLKEN=0, otherwise stay; WDT's GEN goes to 0x02 and its CLKEN to the NVM User Row WDT Enable bit when WRTLOCK=0, otherwise both stay; every other ID's GEN and CLKEN go to 0x00 when WRTLOCK=0, otherwise stay; WRTLOCK never changes on a user reset.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY

fields.name: DIVSEL
fields.text: Chooses how the generator divides its source. For no division, DIVSEL must be 0 and the generator's GENDIV.DIV 0 or 1.

fields.name: OE

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Which generic clock generator is being set up or read. A power reset resets GENCTRL for every ID, including the RTC's generator; a user reset resets it for any generator other than 0 that is not the source of a locked generic clock or of the RTC clock. Power-reset values: 0x00 0x00010600, 0x01 0x00000001, 0x02 0x00010302, 0x03 0x00000003, 0x04 0x00000004, 0x05 0x00000005; after a user reset generator 0 returns to 0x00010600 and generators 1-5 to these values unless used by the RTC or by a GCLK with WRTLOCK at 1, which keep theirs.

fields.name: DIV

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Which generic clock generator the division factor goes to. Power-reset values: 0x00 0x00000000, and generator n (1-5) 0x0000000n; after a user reset generator 0 returns to 0x00000000 and generators 1-5 to 0x0000000n unless used by the RTC or by a GCLK with WRTLOCK at 1, which keep theirs.

values.text: Overflow interrupt on: a request is raised when the overflow flag sets.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Synchronization ready interrupt enable; writing 1 here clears the enable and turns the interrupt off, writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Synchronization ready interrupt on: a request is raised when its flag sets.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Compare x interrupt enable (x = 0..1); writing 1 here clears the enable and turns the interrupt off, writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Compare x interrupt on: a request is raised when its flag sets.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Overflow interrupt enable; writing 1 here sets the enable and turns the interrupt on, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Synchronization ready interrupt enable; writing 1 here sets the enable and turns the interrupt on, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Compare x interrupt enable (x = 0..1); writing 1 here sets the enable and turns the interrupt on, writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear - MODE1

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Overflow flag: goes to 1 one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after the counter overflows, raising an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.OVF is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Synchronization ready flag: goes to 1 when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless that came from an enable or a software reset, raising an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMPx
fields.text: Compare x flag (x = 0..1): goes to 1 one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after a compare match, raising an interrupt when INTENCLR/SET.CMPx is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while registers are being synchronized between clock domains and 0 once that is done.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: 0 stops the RTC while the CPU is halted in debug mode; 1 keeps it running. A software reset leaves this bit alone.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Correction sign.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: Size of the trim made to the RTC prescaler; a value from 1 to 127 adjusts the RTC frequency in line with that value.

fields.name: COUNT
fields.text: Current value of the 16-bit RTC counter.

fields.name: PER
fields.text: Period value of the 16-bit RTC counter.

fields.name: COMP
fields.text: 16-bit compare value, checked against COUNT all the time; on a match INTFLAG.CMPn sets on the following counter cycle.

fields.name: PRESCALER
fields.text: Divides GCLK_RTC by 1 (DIV1) up to 1024 (DIV1024) in powers of two to make the counter clock CLK_RTC_CNT; codes 0xB-0xF are reserved. Not synchronized.

fields.name: MATCHCLR
fields.text: Valid in Mode 0 and Mode 2 only; picks whether a Compare/Alarm 0 match resets the counter. Writable only while the RTC is disabled. Not synchronized.

values.text: Counter keeps running through a Compare/Alarm 0 match.
Counter goes to zero on a Compare/Alarm 0 match.

fields.name: CLKREP
fields.text: Mode 2 only: sets the hour format used in CLOCK. Writable only while the RTC is disabled. Not synchronized.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Selects how the RTC runs: 0x0 COUNT32 counts in 32 bits, 0x1 COUNT16 counts in 16 bits, 0x2 CLOCK keeps date and time; 0x3 is reserved. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the RTC on or off. The written value reads back at once while STATUS.SYNCBUSY goes high; the change takes effect when SYNCBUSY clears. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every RTC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value and disable the RTC; writing 0 does nothing. A 1 here overrides every other write in the same access. The reset finishes after synchronization, when SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both clear. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RREQ
fields.text: Write 1 to start a read synchronization of the register named by READREQ.ADDR, which also sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RCONT
fields.text: 1 keeps the register named by READREQ.ADDR synchronized automatically on every update and stops READREQ.RREQ from self-clearing; 0 turns this off. Cleared by any write to the register named by ADDR.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: Offset of the register to read-synchronize. Only COUNT and CLOCK, at one shared address, can be synchronized in the RTC, so this reads as the fixed value 0x10.

fields.name: OVFEO
fields.text: Overflow event output enable.

values.text: An event goes out on each overflow.

fields.name: ALARMEO0
fields.text: Alarm 0 event output enable.

values.text: An event goes out on each Alarm 0 match.

fields.name: PEREOx
fields.text: Periodic interval x event output enable, one bit per interval x = 0 to 7.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Overflow interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Overflow interrupt on: a request is raised when INTFLAG.OVF sets.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Synchronization Ready interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Synchronization Ready interrupt on: a request is raised when INTFLAG.SYNCRDY sets.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Write 1 to turn off the Alarm 0 interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Alarm 0 interrupt on: a request is raised when INTFLAG.ALARM0 sets.

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Overflow interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Synchronization Ready interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Write 1 to turn on the Alarm 0 interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INTFLAG
registers.title: Interrupt Flag Status and Clear - MODE2

fields.name: OVF
fields.text: Goes high one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after an overflow and raises an interrupt request when the OVF interrupt is enabled. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Goes high when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless the fall came from an enable or a software reset, and raises an interrupt request when the SYNCRDY interrupt is enabled. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ALARM0
fields.text: Goes high one CLK_RTC_CNT cycle after an ALARM0 match and raises an interrupt request when the ALARM0 interrupt is enabled. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: High while registers are being synchronized between the clock domains; goes low when that finishes.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: 0 stops the RTC while the debugger halts the CPU; 1 lets it keep running. A software reset leaves this bit unchanged.

fields.name: SIGN
fields.text: Correction sign.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: How much correction goes to the RTC prescaler; at 1 to 127 the RTC frequency is adjusted in step with the value.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Years past a reference year chosen by software. A year with YEAR[1:0] = 0 counts as a leap year.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Month, 1 (January) to 12 (December).

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Day of the month, from 1 to 28, 29, 30 or 31 according to month and year.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Hour. With CTRL.CLKREP = 0 it counts 0 to 23; with CTRL.CLKREP = 1, HOUR[3:0] counts 1 to 12 and HOUR[4] is 0 for AM, 1 for PM.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Minute, 0 to 59.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Second, 0 to 59.

registers.name: ALARM
registers.title: Alarm n Value - MODE2
notes: CLOCK is checked against ALARM0 continuously, with the fields MASKn.SEL picks; a match sets INTFLAG.ALARMn one counter cycle later and, with CTRL.MATCHCLR = 1, resets the count to zero.

fields.name: YEAR
fields.text: Alarm year; compared only when MASKn.SEL = 6.

fields.name: MONTH
fields.text: Alarm month; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 4.

fields.name: DAY
fields.text: Alarm day; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 3.

fields.name: HOUR
fields.text: Alarm hour; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 2.

fields.name: MINUTE
fields.text: Alarm minute; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 1.

fields.name: SECOND
fields.text: Alarm second; compared only when MASKn.SEL is above 0.

fields.name: SEL
fields.text: Chooses which parts of ALARMn take part in the match: 0x0 OFF (alarm off), 0x1 SS (seconds), 0x2 MMSS (plus minutes), 0x3 HHMMSS (plus hours), 0x4 DDHHMMSS (plus days), 0x5 MMDDHHMMSS (plus months), 0x6 YYMMDDHHMMSS (plus years); 0x7 is reserved.

fields.name: LVLENx
fields.text: Set to pass requests of priority level x to the arbiter; clear to ignore requests at that level. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: CRCENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the CRC module on. Write 0 turns it off only while CRCSTATUS.CRCBUSY is 0; otherwise the write is dropped and the module stays on. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: DMAENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the DMAC on. A 0 written mid-transfer aborts it, but the bit stays set until the internal transfer buffer drains, which happens when the current burst finishes. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1, with both DMAENABLE and CRCENABLE at 0, to return every DMAC register except DBGCTRL to its reset value. With either module on, the request is dropped and the DMAC answers with an access error. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CRCSRC
fields.text: Picks what feeds the CRC: nothing (0x0), the I/O interface (0x1) or DMA channel n (0x20 onward). It is locked, and cannot be changed, while a CRC runs, until the CRC finishes or the module is turned off; CRCBUSY shows the lock. With a DMA channel as source, that source produces and signals CRC completion.

fields.name: CRCPOLY
fields.text: Polynomial: 0x0 CRC-16 (CRC-CCITT), 0x1 CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3); 0x2 and 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: CRCBEATSIZE
fields.text: Width of each bus access when the CRC takes data from the I/O interface: 0x0 byte, 0x1 half-word, 0x2 word; 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: CRCDATAIN
fields.text: Data word to run through the CRC. After a write, the time until the new checksum is ready follows CRCCTRL.CRCBEATSIZE, at one clock cycle per byte.

fields.name: CRCCHKSUM
fields.text: The CRC result. With CRC-16 the upper 16 bits read 0. Read it only when CRCSTATUS.BUSY is 0: then a CRC-16 result is valid as is, and a CRC-32 result is valid but bit-reversed (bit 31 swapped with bit 0, bit 30 with bit 1, and so on).

fields.name: CRCZERO
fields.text: Goes to 1 when a CRC finishes with a zero checksum; goes to 0 when a new CRC source is chosen.

fields.name: CRCBUSY
fields.text: CRC in progress. With the I/O interface as source (CRCSRC 0x1), it sets when CRCDATAIN is written and is cleared by writing 1. With a DMA channel as source (CRCSRC 0x20 to 0x3F), it follows that channel: set when the channel is enabled, cleared when it is disabled, and writing 1 does nothing. Writing 0 never has an effect.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Chooses whether the DMAC keeps running while an external debugger holds the CPU halted. A software reset leaves this bit alone.

values.text: DMAC stops while the CPU is halted by the debugger.
DMAC keeps running while the CPU is halted by the debugger.

fields.name: DQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority for data transfers: 0x0 background, 0x1 bandwidth-sensitive, 0x2 latency-sensitive, 0x3 latency-critical.

fields.name: FQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority for descriptor fetches: 0x0 background, 0x1 bandwidth-sensitive, 0x2 latency-sensitive, 0x3 latency-critical.

fields.name: WRBQOS
fields.text: Memory access priority for write-backs: 0x0 background, 0x1 bandwidth-sensitive, 0x2 latency-sensitive, 0x3 latency-critical.

fields.name: SWTRIGx
fields.text: Write 1 to trigger channel x from software when its CHSTATUS.PEND is 0; if PEND is already 1, the write just sets this bit. The bit clears when CHSTATUS.PEND for the channel goes to 1, or by writing 1 to it; writing 0 also clears it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN3
fields.text: Selects the scheduling scheme for priority-level-3 channels.

fields.name: LVLPRI3
fields.text: With round-robin on at level 3 (RRLVLEN3 = 1): number of the channel last granted access at that level. With static scheduling (RRLVLEN3 = 0) and a non-zero value x: channel x ranks highest, priority falls from x up to the last channel n, then n ranks above channel 0 and priority keeps falling from 0 to x-1. Turning round-robin off does not reset it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN2
fields.text: Selects the scheduling scheme for priority-level-2 channels.

fields.name: LVLPRI2
fields.text: With round-robin on at level 2 (RRLVLEN2 = 1): number of the channel last granted access at that level. With static scheduling (RRLVLEN2 = 0) and a non-zero value x: channel x ranks highest, priority falls from x up to the last channel n, then n ranks above channel 0 and priority keeps falling from 0 to x-1. Turning round-robin off does not reset it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN1
fields.text: Selects the scheduling scheme for priority-level-1 channels.

fields.name: LVLPRI1
fields.text: With round-robin on at level 1 (RRLVLEN1 = 1): number of the channel last granted access at that level. With static scheduling (RRLVLEN1 = 0) and a non-zero value x: channel x ranks highest, priority falls from x up to the last channel n, then n ranks above channel 0 and priority keeps falling from 0 to x-1. Turning round-robin off does not reset it.

fields.name: RRLVLEN0
fields.text: Selects the scheduling scheme for priority-level-0 channels.

fields.name: LVLPRI0
fields.text: With round-robin on at level 0 (RRLVLEN0 = 1): number of the channel last granted access at that level. With static scheduling (RRLVLEN0 = 0) and a non-zero value x: channel x ranks highest, priority falls from x up to the last channel n, then n ranks above channel 0 and priority keeps falling from 0 to x-1. Turning round-robin off does not reset it.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: Reads 1 while the channel named by ID is pending.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: Reads 1 while the channel named by ID is busy.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID fetched an invalid descriptor.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Suspend interrupt waiting. Write 1 to clear that flag; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Transfer Complete interrupt waiting. Write 1 to clear that flag; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Reads 1 when the channel named by ID has a Transfer Error interrupt waiting. Write 1 to clear that flag; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Lowest-numbered channel with an interrupt waiting; valid when SUSP, TCMPL or TERR is set. It updates when a lower channel gets a pending interrupt or when the channel's interrupt sources are cleared, and reads 0 when none are pending. Writing it opens indirect access to that channel's interrupt flag register.

fields.name: CHINTx
fields.text: 1 while channel x has an interrupt waiting; goes to 0 when that channel's interrupts are disabled or their sources cleared.

fields.name: BUSYCHx
fields.text: 1 from the moment channel x starts a transfer; goes to 0 when its trigger action completes, when it hits a bus error, or when it is disabled.

fields.name: PENDCHx
fields.text: 1 while channel x has a transfer pending; goes to 0 when the trigger action set for the channel starts executing, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit block transfer count of the transfer now running. It is held in the active channel and written back to that channel's write-back memory when the arbiter grants another channel. Valid only while ABUSY is 1.

fields.name: ABUSY
fields.text: 1 once the next descriptor's transfer count has been read from write-back memory; 0 once the active count has been written back there.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Index of the channel whose state the active channel registers now hold; refreshed at every new grant by the arbiter.

fields.name: LVLEXx
fields.text: 1 while a trigger request from a level-x channel is pending or running.

fields.name: BASEADDR
fields.text: Base address of descriptor memory; must be 128-bit aligned.

fields.name: WRBADDR
fields.text: Base address of write-back memory; must be 128-bit aligned.

fields.name: ID
fields.text: Number of the channel the channel registers address. Write it before any read or write of a channel register.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Write 1 to turn the channel on. A 0 written mid-transfer aborts it, but the bit stays set until the internal transfer buffer drains, which happens when the current burst finishes. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1, with ENABLE at 0, to return all of this channel's registers to their reset values; the bit clears itself when done. While ENABLE is 1 the write is ignored. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Software command to the channel: 0x0 none, 0x1 suspend, 0x2 resume; 0x3 reserved. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: TRIGACT
fields.text: How much one trigger moves: 0x0 a whole block, 0x2 one beat, 0x3 a whole transaction; 0x1 reserved.

fields.name: TRIGSRC
fields.text: Peripheral trigger that starts the channel's transfers.

values.name: DISABLE
values.text: No peripheral trigger; software or event triggers only.

fields.name: LVL
fields.text: Arbitration level of the channel, 0x0 (level 0) to 0x3 (level 3); a higher level wins over a lower one. 0x4 to 0x7 reserved. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: EVOE
fields.text: Turns on event output from the channel, generated on each condition chosen by the descriptor's BTCTRL.EVOSEL. Present only on channels that support event output.

fields.name: EVIE
fields.text: Turns on event input to the channel. Present only on channels that support event input.

values.text: Incoming events trigger no channel action.
Incoming events run the channel's event action.

fields.name: EVACT
fields.text: Action taken on an incoming event, only when EVIE is 1 and only on channels with event input: 0x0 none, 0x1 transfer or periodic transfer trigger, 0x2 conditional transfer trigger, 0x3 conditional block transfer, 0x4 suspend channel, 0x5 resume channel, 0x6 skip the next block suspend action; 0x7 reserved.

values.name: TRIG
values.text: Event triggers a transfer or periodic transfer.

values.name: CTRIG
values.text: Event is a conditional transfer trigger.

values.name: SSKIP
values.text: Event skips the next block suspend action.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Channel Suspend interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Transfer Complete interrupt; writing 0 does nothing. With the block action set to none, the TCMPL flag is not set when a block finishes.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Transfer Error interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Channel Suspend interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Transfer Complete interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Transfer Error interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHINTFLAG
registers.title: Channel Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: SUSP
fields.text: Set when a block with the suspend block action finishes, when a software suspend command runs, when a suspend event arrives, or on an invalid descriptor fetch. Write 1 to clear it for this channel; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TCMPL
fields.text: Set when a block finishes and its block action includes the interrupt. Write 1 to clear it for this channel; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TERR
fields.text: Set on a bus error during a beat or on an invalid descriptor fetch. Write 1 to clear it for this channel; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: 1 after an invalid descriptor is fetched; cleared when a software resume command runs.

fields.name: BUSY
fields.text: 1 from the moment the channel starts a transfer; goes to 0 when its trigger action completes, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: PEND
fields.text: 1 while the channel has a transfer pending; goes to 0 when the trigger action set for the channel starts executing, on a bus error, or when the channel is disabled.

fields.name: STEPSIZE
fields.text: Address step after each beat, in units of BEATSIZE: 0x0 x1, 0x1 x2, 0x2 x4, 0x3 x8, 0x4 x16, 0x5 x32, 0x6 x64, 0x7 x128. STEPSEL picks whether it applies to the source or the destination address.

values.name: X1
values.text: Next address is the current one plus 1 times BEATSIZE.

values.name: X2
values.text: Next address is the current one plus 2 times BEATSIZE.

values.name: X4
values.text: Next address is the current one plus 4 times BEATSIZE.

values.name: X8
values.text: Next address is the current one plus 8 times BEATSIZE.

values.name: X16
values.text: Next address is the current one plus 16 times BEATSIZE.

values.name: X32
values.text: Next address is the current one plus 32 times BEATSIZE.

values.name: X64
values.text: Next address is the current one plus 64 times BEATSIZE.

values.name: X128
values.text: Next address is the current one plus 128 times BEATSIZE.

fields.name: STEPSEL
fields.text: Which address uses STEPSIZE: 0x0 the destination, 0x1 the source.

values.name: DST
values.text: Step size acts on the destination address.

values.name: SRC
values.text: Step size acts on the source address.

fields.name: DSTINC
fields.text: Write 1 to make the destination address advance during the transfer, by 1 unless STEPSEL is 0, when STEPSIZE sets the step; write 0 to hold it fixed.

fields.name: SRCINC
fields.text: Write 1 to make the source address advance during the transfer, by 1 unless STEPSEL is 1, when STEPSIZE sets the step; write 0 to hold it fixed.

fields.name: BEATSIZE
fields.text: Size of one beat, the width of each bus read and write: 0x0 8 bits, 0x1 16 bits, 0x2 32 bits; 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: BLOCKACT
fields.text: What the DMAC does when a block finishes: 0x0 nothing, 0x1 block interrupt with the channel running on, 0x2 suspend the channel, 0x3 suspend the channel and raise the block interrupt.

values.name: INT
values.text: Channel keeps running and raises the block interrupt.

values.name: BOTH
values.text: Channel suspends and raises the block interrupt.

fields.name: EVOSEL
fields.text: When the channel emits an event: 0x0 never, 0x1 at each completed block, 0x3 at each completed beat; 0x2 reserved.

values.name: BLOCK
values.text: Event strobe at the end of each block transfer.

values.name: BEAT
values.text: Event strobe at the end of each beat transfer.

fields.name: VALID
fields.text: Marks the descriptor as usable. A 0 here in descriptor or write-back memory suspends the channel when it fetches this descriptor. The DMAC clears it in write-back memory when the channel is aborted, on an error during the block, or when the block completes.

fields.name: BTCNT
fields.text: 16-bit block transfer count. The internal counter drops by one per beat and is copied to the channel's write-back memory when the channel loses priority, is suspended, or is disabled (by finishing, by a transfer error, or by software).

fields.name: SRCADDR
fields.text: Source address of the last beat of the block.

fields.name: DSTADDR
fields.text: Destination address of the last beat of the block.

fields.name: DESCADDR
fields.text: SRAM address of the next descriptor; must be 128-bit aligned. A value of 0x00000000 ends the transaction when the DMAC goes to load the next descriptor.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the EIC on or off. The written value reads back at once and STATUS.SYNCBUSY is set; the EIC is turned on or off after synchronization, when SYNCBUSY clears.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every EIC register to its reset value and turn the EIC off; it overrides any other write in the same access. Reset completes after synchronization, when SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both clear. Writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: 1 while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; 0 once that finishes.

fields.name: NMIFILTEN
fields.text: Non-maskable interrupt filter enable.

fields.name: NMISENSE
fields.text: Edge or level that triggers the NMI: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

registers.name: NMIFLAG
registers.title: Non-Maskable Interrupt Flag Status and Clear

fields.name: NMI
fields.text: Set when the NMI pin meets the NMISENSE condition, raising an interrupt request. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTEOx
fields.text: Turns on an event from pin EXTINTx at each detection.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Write 1 to disable external interrupt x; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Write 1 to enable external interrupt x; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EXTINTx
fields.text: Set when pin EXTINTx meets its sense condition; it then requests an interrupt when the matching EXTINT[x] enable bit (INTENCLR/INTENSET) is 1. Write 1 to clear it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WAKEUPENx
fields.text: Lets pin EXTINTx wake the device from sleep when it meets its sense condition.

values.text: EXTINTx does not wake the device.

registers.name: CONFIG
registers.title: Configuration n
notes: The heading for FILTENx leaves out bit 3, the diagram's FILTEN0.
The heading for SENSEx leaves out bits 2:0, the diagram's SENSE0.
Also listed under the name CONFIG0.

fields.name: FILTEN7
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+7].

fields.name: SENSE7
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+7] raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN6
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+6].

fields.name: SENSE6
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+6] raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN5
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+5].

fields.name: SENSE5
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+5] raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN4
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+4].

fields.name: SENSE4
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+4] raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN3
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+3].

fields.name: SENSE3
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+3] raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN2
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+2].

fields.name: SENSE2
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+2] raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN1
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+1].

fields.name: SENSE1
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+1] raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: FILTEN0
fields.text: Filter enable for input EXTINT[n*8+0].

fields.name: SENSE0
fields.text: Edge or level on which EXTINT[n*8+0] raises its interrupt or event: 0x0 none, 0x1 rising edge, 0x2 falling edge, 0x3 both edges, 0x4 high level, 0x5 low level; 0x6 and 0x7 reserved.

fields.name: CMDEX
fields.text: Key for running the command in CMD: 0xA5 lets it run, written in the same access as CMD; any other key, or a write while an earlier command is unfinished, drops the write and sets PROGE. READY must be 1 when the command is issued. An APB command that coincides with an AHB access waits until the AHB access and the NVM block are idle. Bit 0 reads 1 until the command has been issued.

values.name: KEY
values.text: Key that lets the command run.

fields.name: CMD
fields.text: Command that runs when the CMDEX key is written.

values.name: ER
values.text: Erase Row: erases the row at the address in ADDR.

values.name: WP
values.text: Write Page: writes the page buffer into the page at the address in ADDR.

values.name: EAR
values.text: Erase Auxiliary Row: erases the auxiliary row at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear, and only for the user configuration row.

values.name: WAP
values.text: Write Auxiliary Page: writes the page buffer into the auxiliary page at the address in ADDR; accepted only while the security bit is clear, and only for the user configuration row.

values.name: LR
values.text: Lock Region: locks the region holding the address in ADDR.

values.name: UR
values.text: Unlock Region: unlocks the region holding the address in ADDR.

values.name: SPRM
values.text: SPRM: turn power reduction mode on.

values.name: CPRM
values.text: CPRM: turn power reduction mode off.

values.name: SSB
values.text: Set Security Bit: a 0x00 is written into the first byte of the lockbit row, which turns the security bit on.

fields.name: CACHEDIS
fields.text: Turns the NVM cache off when set.

fields.name: READMODE
fields.text: Cache read mode. 0x0 NO_MISS_PENALTY: no wait state on a cache miss; the highest system performance. 0x1 LOW_POWER: lower cache power, but each miss adds a wait state that stalls the application and can lengthen run time, so it may not suit code that needs CPU performance. 0x2 DETERMINISTIC: a hit and a miss take equal time, set by the programmed flash wait states; for real-time code that needs deterministic timing. 0x3 is reserved.

values.name: NO_MISS_PENALTY
values.text: No wait state is added on a cache miss; best system performance.

values.name: LOW_POWER
values.text: Lower cache power, with one wait state added on every cache miss; the stalled CPU can make run time longer.

values.name: DETERMINISTIC
values.text: Cache hits and misses take equal time, set by the programmed flash wait states; for real-time code needing fixed timing.

fields.name: SLEEPPRM
fields.text: How the NVM block saves power in sleep. 0x0 WAKEONACCESS: low-power on entering sleep, out of it on the first access. 0x1 WAKEUPINSTANT: low-power on entering sleep, out of it on leaving sleep. 0x3 DISABLED: no automatic power reduction. 0x2 is reserved.

values.name: WAKEONACCESS
values.text: NVM goes to low power on sleep and leaves it at the first access.

values.name: WAKEUPINSTANT
values.text: NVM goes to low power on sleep and leaves it on wake from sleep.

fields.name: MANW
fields.text: Selects whether page writes start on their own or only by command; covers main memory and auxiliary rows.

values.text: A write to the last word of the page buffer starts writing the page at the last written address.
Writes start only from a command in CMD.

fields.name: RWS
fields.text: Number of wait states added to an NVM read, 0 to 15; resets to 0. Software sets it to suit the NVM access time and the system clock frequency.

fields.name: PSZ
fields.text: Size of one NVM page: codes 0x0 to 0x7 give 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 and 1024 bytes. A device family need not offer every size.

fields.name: NVMP
fields.text: How many pages the NVM main address space holds.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Reads back the ERROR interrupt enable; writing 1 turns it off, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Reads back the READY interrupt enable; writing 1 turns it off, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Reads back the ERROR interrupt enable; writing 1 turns it on, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: Reads back the READY interrupt enable; writing 1 turns it on, writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Goes to 1 when an NVME, LOCKE or PROGE error occurs; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: No error since the flag was last cleared.
One or more errors since the flag was last cleared.

fields.name: READY
fields.text: NVM ready flag.

values.text: Controller busy with a program or erase.
Controller can take a new command.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Security bit state.

fields.name: NVME
fields.text: NVM programming or erase error flag; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: The NVM controller has reported no program or erase error since the last clear.
The NVM controller has reported one or more errors since the last clear.

fields.name: LOCKE
fields.text: Lock error flag; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: No locked region has been programmed since the last clear.
One or more locked regions have been programmed since the last clear.

fields.name: PROGE
fields.text: Programming error flag; writing 1 clears it.

values.text: No invalid command or wrong key has been written to the command register since the last clear.
An invalid command, a wrong key, or both have been written to the command register since the last clear.

fields.name: LOAD
fields.text: Goes to 1 as soon as one or more words are loaded into the NVM page buffer and holds there until a page is written or the PBCLR command empties the buffer; writing 1 also clears it.

fields.name: PRM
fields.text: Shows whether the NVM is in power reduction mode. It enters that mode by command or on entering sleep under the matching SLEEPPRM setting, and leaves it on an AHB access to the NVM block, by command (SPRM, CPRM), or on leaving sleep under the matching SLEEPPRM setting.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: The 16-bit hardware address given to the NVM when CMDEX runs a command; a byte address goes in shifted right by one. Written by hand, or updated automatically on page buffer writes; it is the offset within the addressed section.

fields.name: LOCK
fields.text: One bit per lock region; changed only through commands in CMD.

registers.name: DIRn
registers.title: Data Direction
notes: Also listed under the name DIR.

fields.name: DIR
fields.text: One bit per pin of the group, setting its direction.

registers.name: DIRCLRn
registers.title: Data Direction Clear
notes: Also listed under the name DIRCLR.

fields.name: DIRCLR
fields.text: Writing 1 to a bit clears that bit of DIR, making the pin an input; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: DIRSETn
registers.title: Data Direction Set
notes: Also listed under the name DIRSET.

fields.name: DIRSET
fields.text: Writing 1 to a bit sets that bit of DIR, making the pin an output; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: DIRTGLn
registers.title: Data Direction Toggle
notes: Also listed under the name DIRTGL.

fields.name: DIRTGL
fields.text: Writing 1 to a bit flips that bit of DIR, swapping the pin's direction; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: OUTn
registers.title: Data Output Value
notes: Also listed under the name OUT.

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: Level driven on each pin that DIR makes an output; on a DIR input with PULLEN set, chooses whether the pull is up or down.

values.text: Output low, or input pulled down.
Output high, or input pulled up.

registers.name: OUTCLRn
registers.title: Data Output Value Clear
notes: Also listed under the name OUTCLR.

fields.name: OUTCLR
fields.text: Writing 1 to a bit clears that bit of OUT: a DIR output drives low, and a DIR input with PULLEN set is pulled down. Writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: OUTSETn
registers.title: Data Output Value Set
notes: Also listed under the name OUTSET.

fields.name: OUTSET
fields.text: Writing 1 to a bit sets that bit of OUT: a DIR output drives high, and a DIR input with PULLEN set is pulled up. Writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: OUTTGLn
registers.title: Data Output Value Toggle
notes: Also listed under the name OUTTGL.

fields.name: OUTTGL
fields.text: Writing 1 to a bit flips that bit of OUT: a DIR output swaps level, and a DIR input with PULLEN set swaps its pull direction. Writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: INn
registers.title: Data Input Value
notes: Also listed under the name IN.

fields.name: IN
fields.text: Each bit reads 0 when the pin's input sampler sees a low level and 1 when it sees a high level.

registers.name: CTRLn
registers.title: Control
notes: Also listed under the name CTRL.

fields.name: SAMPLING
fields.text: Sets input sampling for pins that DIR makes inputs. Samplers switch on and off in blocks of eight pins, so one pin in a byte asking for continuous sampling makes all eight sample continuously.

registers.name: WRCONFIGn
registers.title: Write Configuration
notes: Also listed under the name WRCONFIG.
Write-only: it sets the configuration and peripheral multiplexing of several pins at once. Only a 32-bit write takes effect; an 8- or 16-bit write does nothing. Reads return 0.

fields.name: HWSEL
fields.text: Picks which 16-pin half of the 32-pin group the atomic write changes; reads 0.

fields.name: WRPINCFG
fields.text: Writing 1 makes the atomic write load the written DRVSTR, SLEWLIM, ODRAIN, PULLEN, INEN, PMUXEN and PINMASK values into PINCFGy of every pin picked by PINMASK and HWSEL; writing 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

values.text: PINCFGy of the picked pins left unchanged.
PINCFGy of the picked pins updated.

fields.name: WRPMUX
fields.text: Writing 1 makes the atomic write load the written WRCONFIG.PMUX value into PMUXn for every pin picked by PINMASK and HWSEL; writing 0 does nothing. Reads 0.

values.text: PMUXn of the picked pins left unchanged.
PMUXn of the picked pins updated.

fields.name: PMUX
fields.text: Value loaded into PMUXn of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPMUX is set; reads 0.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Value loaded into PINCFGy.DRVSTR of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is set; reads 0.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Value loaded into PINCFGy.PULLEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is set; reads 0.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Value loaded into PINCFGy.INEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is set; reads 0.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Value loaded into PINCFGy.PMUXEN of the pins picked by PINMASK and HWSEL when WRPINCFG is set; reads 0.

fields.name: PINMASK
fields.text: One bit per pin of the half chosen by HWSEL, marking the pins the atomic write changes; reads 0.

fields.name: PMUXO
fields.text: Peripheral function of the odd pin (2n+1) of the group, used when that pin's PINCFGy.PMUXEN is 1: 0x0 to 0x7 pick functions A to H; 0x8 to 0xF are reserved. Some codes may not be valid.

fields.name: PMUXE
fields.text: Peripheral function of the even pin (2n) of the group, used when that pin's PINCFGy.PMUXEN is 1: 0x0 to 0x7 pick functions A to H; 0x8 to 0xF are reserved. Some codes may not be valid.

fields.name: DRVSTR
fields.text: Drive strength of the pin when it is an output.

fields.name: PULLEN
fields.text: Turns on the internal pull-up or pull-down of the pin when it is an input.

values.text: Pull off; input floats at high impedance.
Pull on; input held at a known level when nothing drives it.

fields.name: INEN
fields.text: Turns the pin's input buffer on or off, whether the pin is an input or an output; with it off, the pin's level cannot be read back.

values.text: Input buffer off; the pin is not sampled.
Input buffer on; the pin is sampled when needed.

fields.name: PMUXEN
fields.text: Hands control of the pin's direction and output level to the peripheral chosen in PMUXn. With 0, PORT drives the pad from DIR and OUT and PMUXn is ignored; with 1, the peripheral drives it, and IN still reads the pin when PINCFGy.INEN is set.

values.text: Peripheral selection off; PORT registers set direction and output level.
Peripheral selection on; the chosen peripheral sets direction and output level.

fields.name: GCLKREQ
fields.text: Chooses whether each channel's generic clock runs continuously or is started only on demand by an event. Events on asynchronous paths need no generic clock.

values.text: The channel's generic clock is asked for and switched on only once an event is seen.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Writing 1 returns every EVSYS register to its reset value, and any other write in the same access is ignored; writing 0 does nothing.

registers.name: CHANNEL
registers.title: Channel
notes: Configures the channel named in CHANNEL.CHANNEL. A write carries the whole configuration and the channel number in one 32-bit access; to read a channel's configuration, first write its number to CHANNEL.CHANNEL with an 8-bit access, then read CHANNEL.

fields.name: EDGSEL
fields.text: Edge detection on the channel, for the synchronous or resynchronized path. 0x0 NO_EVT_OUTPUT: no event output. 0x1 RISING_EDGE: rising edges of the generator's signal only. 0x2 FALLING_EDGE: falling edges only. 0x3 BOTH_EDGES: both edges. Must be 0 on the asynchronous path.

values.name: NO_EVT_OUTPUT
values.text: No event output on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

values.name: RISING_EDGE
values.text: Rising edge of the generator's signal, on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

values.name: FALLING_EDGE
values.text: Falling edge of the generator's signal, on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

values.name: BOTH_EDGES
values.text: Both edges of the generator's signal, on the resynchronized or synchronous path.

fields.name: PATH
fields.text: Path the channel uses: SYNCHRONOUS, RESYNCHRONIZED or ASYNCHRONOUS; 0x3 is reserved. The channel source can limit which paths are allowed.

fields.name: EVGEN
fields.text: Event generator connected to the channel.

rows: Compare 0 in modes 0 and 1, alarm 0 in mode 2.

fields.name: SWEVT
fields.text: Writing 1 fires a software event on the channel named by CHANNEL.CHANNEL; it must go in the same 16-bit write as CHANNEL.CHANNEL. Writing 0 does nothing; reads 0.

fields.name: CHANNEL
fields.text: Channel being configured or read.

registers.name: USER
registers.title: User Multiplexer
notes: Configures the event user named in USER.USER. A write carries the whole configuration and the user number in one 16-bit access; to read a user's configuration, first write its number to USER.USER with an 8-bit access, then read USER.

fields.name: CHANNEL
fields.text: Channel connected to the event user; channel n is chosen by writing n+1. 0x0 connects no channel; 0x1 to 0x5 pick channels 0 to 4.

fields.name: USER
fields.text: Event user being connected to a channel, or whose channel value is read.

fields.name: CHBUSYx
fields.text: Reads 1 while an event on channel x has not yet been taken by every event user on it, and 0 when the channel is idle.

fields.name: USRRDYx
fields.text: Reads 1 when every event user on channel x is ready for events on it, and 0 when any of them is not ready.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the channel x event detected interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Channel x event detected interrupt off.
Channel x event detected interrupt on.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: Writing 1 clears the channel x overrun interrupt enable, disabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the channel x event detected interrupt enable, enabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Channel x event detected interrupt off.
Channel x event detected interrupt on.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: Writing 1 sets the channel x overrun interrupt enable, enabling that interrupt; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EVDx
fields.text: Goes to 1 one CLK_EVSYS_APB cycle after an event starts passing through channel x, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.EVDx is 1; stays 0 on an asynchronous path. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVRx
fields.text: Goes to 1 one CLK_EVSYS cycle after channel x overruns, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.OVRx is 1; stays 0 on an asynchronous path. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

peripherals.name: SERCOM USART
peripherals.title: SERCOM Universal Synchronous and Asynchronous Receiver and Transmitter

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Bit order of each character shifted out of the Data register. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: In synchronous mode, selects which XCK edge changes TxD and which samples RxD. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CMODE
fields.text: Picks asynchronous or synchronous operation. Not synchronized.

fields.name: FORM
fields.text: Selects the frame format. Not synchronized.

values.text: USART frame with a parity bit.
Auto-baud with parity: break detection and auto-baud.

fields.name: SAMPA
fields.text: Chooses which three over-sampled positions are used for the bit decision. Not synchronized.

fields.name: RXPO
fields.text: Selects the pad that carries received data (RxD). Not synchronized.

fields.name: TXPO
fields.text: Selects the pads for TxD and XCK, and for RTS and CTS where used. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SAMPR
fields.text: Sets the over-sampling rate and the baud generation method. Not synchronized.

fields.name: IBON
fields.text: Chooses when STATUS.BUFOVF is raised after a receive buffer overflow.

values.text: BUFOVF set at the overflowed character's place in the data stream.
BUFOVF set as soon as the overflow happens.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Behaviour in standby sleep. Not synchronized. 0x0: with an external clock, the clock is disconnected once the ongoing transfer ends and all reception is dropped; with the internal clock, the generic clock stops once the ongoing transfer ends and Receive Start or Transfer Complete can wake the device. 0x1: with an external clock, Receive Start or Receive Complete wakes the device; with the internal clock, the generic clock runs in every sleep mode and any interrupt can wake the device.

rows: The external clock is cut once the ongoing transfer ends; all reception is dropped.
The generic clock stops once the ongoing transfer ends; a Receive Start or Transfer Complete interrupt is able to wake the device.
The Receive Start or Receive Complete interrupt wakes the device.
The generic clock runs in every sleep mode; any interrupt can wake the device.

fields.name: MODE
fields.text: Write 0x0 or 0x1 to make the SERCOM a USART. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the SERCOM on or off. The written value reads back at once while SYNCBUSY.ENABLE is set, and the change takes effect when SYNCBUSY.ENABLE clears. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Write 1 to return every SERCOM register but DBGCTRL to its reset value and disable the SERCOM; writing 0 does nothing. The reset wins over any other write in the same access, register writes during it give an APB error and reads return reset values. CTRLA.SWRST and SYNCBUSY.SWRST clear when it finishes. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: RXEN
fields.text: Turns the receiver on or off. Writing 0 turns it off, empties the receive buffer and clears STATUS.FERR, PERR and BUFOVF. Writing 1 with the USART disabled sets the bit at once; with the USART enabled, SYNCBUSY.CTRLB is set until the receiver is on, and the bit then reads 1. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Receiver on, or on once the USART is enabled.

fields.name: TXEN
fields.text: Turns the transmitter on or off. Writing 0 turns it off only after ongoing and pending transmissions finish. Writing 1 with the USART disabled sets the bit at once; with the USART enabled, SYNCBUSY.CTRLB is set until the transmitter is on, and the bit then reads 1. Not enable-protected.

values.text: Transmitter on, or on once the USART is enabled.

fields.name: PMODE
fields.text: Parity type used when parity is on (CTRLA.FORM 0x1). The transmitter adds parity to each frame; the receiver checks incoming parity and sets STATUS.PERR on a mismatch. Not synchronized.

fields.name: ENC
fields.text: Selects the data encoding. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SFDE
fields.text: Lets the start-of-frame detector wake the device on a start bit seen on RxD; the wake source depends on INTENSET.RXS and INTENSET.RXC. Not synchronized.

values.text: Detection on; RXC wakes the device from any sleep mode (INTENSET.RXS=0, RXC=1).
Detection on; RXS wakes the device from any sleep mode (INTENSET.RXS=1, RXC=0).
Detection on; RXC and RXS each wake the device from any sleep mode (INTENSET.RXS=1, RXC=1).

fields.name: COLDEN
fields.text: Turns collision detection on: 0 off, 1 on. Not synchronized.

fields.name: SBMODE
fields.text: Number of stop bits sent. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CHSIZE
fields.text: Bits per character. Not synchronized.

fields.name: FP[2:0]/BAUD
fields.text: Fractional part of the baud setting, used in clock generation when fractional baud generation is selected (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=1).

fields.name: BAUD
fields.text: Baud value used in clock generation. With fractional baud generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=1) it is bits 12:0; with arithmetic baud generation (CTRLA.SAMPR[0]=0) it is bits 15:0.

fields.name: RXPL
fields.text: With IrDA encoding (CTRLB.ENC=1), sets the shortest pulse the IrDA receiver accepts, in serial engine clock periods: PULSE >= (RXPL + 1) x SE period.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Error interrupt by clearing its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Receive Break interrupt by clearing its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Clear To Send Input Change interrupt by clearing its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off.
Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Receive Start interrupt by clearing its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Receive Complete interrupt by clearing its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Transmit Complete interrupt by clearing its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to disable the Data Register Empty interrupt by clearing its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Error interrupt by setting its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Receive Break interrupt by setting its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Clear To Send Input Change interrupt by setting its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

values.text: Clear To Send Input Change interrupt off.
Clear To Send Input Change interrupt on.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Receive Start interrupt by setting its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Receive Complete interrupt by setting its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Transmit Complete interrupt by setting its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Write 1 to enable the Data Register Empty interrupt by setting its enable bit; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set on any error that has its own STATUS flag: COLL, ISF, BUFOVF, FERR or PERR. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXBRK
fields.text: Set when a break character arrives with auto-baud selected in CTRLA.FORM. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTSIC
fields.text: Set when the CTS pin changes. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXS
fields.text: Set when a start condition is seen on RxD with CTRLB.SFDE set. Write 1 to clear; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RXC
fields.text: Set while DATA holds unread data; cleared by reading DATA or disabling the receiver. Writes have no effect.

fields.name: TXC
fields.text: Set when the whole frame has left the transmit shift register and DATA holds nothing new. Cleared by writing 1 or by writing new data to DATA; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: DRE
fields.text: Set when DATA is empty and can take a write; cleared by writing new data to DATA. Writes to the bit have no effect.

fields.name: COLL
fields.text: Set when a collision is detected with CTRLB.COLDEN set. Cleared by writing 1 or by disabling the receiver; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: ISF
fields.text: Set when, with auto-baud selected in CTRLA.FORM, a sync field other than 0x55 is received. Cleared by writing 1 or by disabling the receiver; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTS
fields.text: With flow control selected in CTRLA.TXPO, reads the CTS pin's present state. Writes have no effect.

fields.name: BUFOVF
fields.text: Read before DATA, it gives the error status of the next character. Set on a buffer overflow, which happens when a further start bit arrives while the receive buffer is full and another character already sits in the shift register. Cleared by writing 1 or by disabling the receiver; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: FERR
fields.text: Read before DATA, it gives the error status of the next character. Set when the received character's first stop bit is 0. Cleared by writing 1 or by disabling the receiver; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: PERR
fields.text: Read before DATA, it gives the error status of the next character. Set on a parity error while parity checking is on (CTRLA.FORM 0x1 or 0x5). Cleared by writing 1 or by disabling the receiver; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: CTRLB
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLB, made with the SERCOM enabled, is being synchronized; writing CTRLB again while it is set gives an APB error.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized; meanwhile writes to any register except CTRLA.SWRST are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized; meanwhile writes to any register are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: A read returns the Receive Data register, and should be made only with INTFLAG.RXC set, after reading STATUS for any error on that character. A write goes to the Transmit Data register, and should be made only with INTFLAG.DRE set.

fields.name: DBGSTOP
fields.text: Sets what the baud-rate generator does while an external debugger halts the CPU.

fields.name: DORD
fields.text: Bit order of each character shifted out of the Data register. Not synchronized.

fields.name: CPOL
fields.text: Idle level of SCK; with CPHA it sets the SPI transfer mode. Not synchronized.

values.text: SCK idles low; leading edge rising, trailing edge falling.
SCK idles high; leading edge falling, trailing edge rising.

fields.name: CPHA
fields.text: Which SCK edge samples and which changes data; with CPOL it sets the SPI transfer mode: mode 0x0 (CPOL 0, CPHA 0) samples on rising, changes on falling; 0x1 (0, 1) changes on rising, samples on falling; 0x2 (1, 0) samples on falling, changes on rising; 0x3 (1, 1) changes on falling, samples on rising. Not synchronized.

values.text: Sample on the leading edge, change on the trailing edge.
Sample on the trailing edge, change on the leading edge.

fields.name: FORM
fields.text: Selects the frame format; with an address format, the first byte received is compared with ADDR.

fields.name: DIPO

fields.name: CMD

fields.name: DRDY

fields.name: AMATCH
fields.text: Set when the address match logic receives a valid address. Hardware clears it when CTRLB.CMD is written; writing 1 also clears it, and writing 0 does nothing. On clearing, ACK or NACK goes out as CTRLB.ACKACT says.

fields.name: PREC
fields.text: Set when a STOP is seen during a transaction the slave is handling; a STOP between the master and some other slave does not set it. Hardware clears it after a command is given on the next address match. Writing 1 also clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: HS

fields.name: SEXTTOUT

fields.name: CLKHOLD

fields.name: LOWTOUT

It raises no interrupt, so software reads it to check the data went out. Cleared on its own by answering an address match with ACK or NACK (0x3 to CTRLB.CMD) or by clearing INTFLAG.AMATCH. fields.name: ACKACT

fields.name: CMD

The acknowledge action applies only when the master reads; when it writes, a command gives only a repeated START or a STOP. ACKACT may be written together with CMD, and is updated before the command runs. Commands are accepted only while INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB is 1. 0x0: no action. 0x1 (either direction): acknowledge action, then a repeated START and the address already in ADDR.ADDR; for another address, write ADDR.ADDR instead of CMD, which gives a repeated START and the new address. 0x2: on a write, nothing; on a read, acknowledge action then a byte read. 0x3 (either direction): acknowledge action, then a STOP. A command sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY. Not enable-protected.

fields.name: ERROR
fields.text: Set when an error is found. The errors are LENERR, SEXTTOUT, MEXTTOUT, LOWTOUT, ARBLOST or BUSERR, and each has its own flag in STATUS. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SB
fields.text: Set when the master receives a byte in master read mode without lost arbitration or bus error; the master then holds SCL low, stretching the clock. SCL is let go and the flag cleared by a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with smart mode on (CTRLB.SMEN), or a valid command written to CTRLB.CMD. Writing 1 clears SB too; writing 0 does nothing. The transaction neither goes on nor ends until one of those actions.

fields.name: MB
fields.text: Set when the master sends a byte in master write mode, whether or not a bus error or lost arbitration happened; also set when arbitration is lost while sending a NACK in master read mode, and when a START is issued with the bus state unknown. While set without lost arbitration, the master holds SCL low, stretching the clock. SCL is let go and the flag cleared by a write to ADDR.ADDR, a write to DATA.DATA, a read of DATA.DATA with smart mode on (CTRLB.SMEN), or a valid command written to CTRLB.CMD. Writing 1 clears MB too, whether or not arbitration was lost; writing 0 does nothing. The transaction neither goes on nor ends until one of those actions.

fields.name: LENERR
fields.text: Set when, with automatic length used for a DMA transaction, the slave sends NACK before the master has written ADDR.LEN bytes. Cleared on its own when ADDR is written. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SEXTTOUT
fields.text: Set when a slave SCL low extend time-out happens. Normal use does not need it cleared by writing 1. Cleared on its own when ADDR is written. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: MEXTTOUT
fields.text: Set when a master SCL low time-out happens. Normal use does not need it cleared by writing 1. Cleared on its own when ADDR is written. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: CLKHOLD
fields.text: Set while the master holds SCL low to stretch the clock. It is a read-only status, set together with INTFLAG.SB or INTFLAG.MB, and cleared once that interrupt flag is cleared and a following operation starts. Writes of 0 or 1 do nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: LOWTOUT
fields.text: Set when an SCL low time-out happens. Normal use does not need it cleared by writing 1. Cleared on its own when ADDR is written. Writing 1 clears it; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSSTATE
fields.text: Shows the I2C bus state; it is unknown after the master is enabled and whenever the master is disabled. 0x0 Unknown: the master waits to see a STOP or to be forced to idle by software. 0x1 Idle: waiting for a transaction to start. 0x2 Owner: this master owns the bus. 0x3 Busy: another master owns the bus. From unknown, writing 0x1 forces the state to idle; no other state can be forced. Writing idle sets STATUS.SYNCBUSY.

values.name: Unknown
values.text: Unknown: the master waits until it sees a stop condition or software forces the bus to idle.

values.name: Idle
values.text: Idle: no transaction has started on the bus.

values.name: Owner
values.text: Owner: this master holds the bus.

values.name: Busy
values.text: Busy: another master holds the bus.

fields.name: RXNACK
fields.text: Tells whether the slave acknowledged the last address or data packet sent. Writes of 0 or 1 do nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: ARBLOST
fields.text: Set when arbitration is lost while sending a high data bit or a NACK, or during a START or repeated START; INTFLAG.MB is set with it. A write to ADDR.ADDR clears it, as does writing 1; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: BUSERR
fields.text: Set when an illegal condition appears on the bus, whoever owns it: a START, repeated START or STOP that breaks the protocol (a START straight followed by a STOP is one), or a time-out during a frame. If the master owns the bus when it happens, STATUS.ARBLOST and INTFLAG.MB are set too. A write to ADDR.ADDR clears it, as does writing 1; writing 0 does nothing. Not write-synchronized.

fields.name: SYSOP
fields.text: Set to 1 while a write to CTRLB, STATUS.BUSSTATE, ADDR or DATA made with the SERCOM enabled is being synchronized, back to 0 when it is done.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Set to 1 while a write to CTRLA.ENABLE is being synchronized, back to 0 when it is done. While it is 1, writes to any register other than CTRLA.SWRST are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: Set to 1 while a write to CTRLA.SWRST is being synchronized, back to 0 when it is done. While it is 1, writes to any register are dropped and give an APB error.

fields.name: LEN
fields.text: Number of bytes in a DMA transaction, 0 to 255. Used only when ADDR.LENEN is 1. Once LEN bytes have gone out or come in, a NACK (on master reads) and a STOP are generated.

fields.name: TENBITEN
fields.text: Turns on 10-bit addressing. May be written together with ADDR to choose a 10-bit or 7-bit address transfer.

fields.name: HS
fields.text: Turns on High-speed mode for the present transfer, from repeated START to STOP. May be written together with ADDR for a high-speed transfer.

fields.name: LENEN
fields.text: Turns on automatic transfer length.

fields.name: ADDR
fields.text: A write starts an operation that depends on the bus state. When unknown: INTFLAG.MB and STATUS.BUSERR go to 1 and the operation ends. When busy: the master waits for the bus to go idle. When idle: the master sends a START and the address; if it is acknowledged, SCL is kept low and both STATUS.CLKHOLD and INTFLAG.MB go to 1. When owner: a repeated START is made, preceded by the acknowledge action if the last transaction was a read; this write is made while INTFLAG.MB or INTFLAG.SB is 1. The whole address is sent whether arbitration is won or lost; after a loss only ones are sent for the rest of it. The write clears the flags BUSERR and ARBLOST in STATUS and MB and SB in INTFLAG. Reading ADDR at any time leaves the bus alone. Bit 0 is the R/W bit: 0 write, 1 read.

fields.name: LEFTADJ
fields.text: Left-aligns the result in RESULT, putting the top byte of a 12-bit result in its upper half; 0, the reset value, right-aligns it. Writable only with the ADC off.

values.text: Left-aligned; high byte of the 12-bit result in the upper byte.

fields.name: DIFFMODE
fields.text: Converts the difference between the MUXPOS and MUXNEG inputs instead of a single input. Writable only with the ADC off.

fields.name: WINMODE
fields.text: Turns on the window monitor and sets its test: 0x0 off (reset); 0x1 RESULT above WINLT; 0x2 RESULT below WINUT; 0x3 RESULT between WINLT and WINUT; 0x4 RESULT not between them; 0x5 to 0x7 reserved.

values.name: MODE4
values.text: RESULT not between WINLT and WINUT.

fields.name: START
fields.text: A 1 starts a conversion and hardware clears the bit once it has begun; a 1 while already set, or a 0, does nothing.

values.text: Starts a conversion; cleared by hardware when it begins.

fields.name: FLUSH
fields.text: A 1 flushes the ADC pipeline: the ADC clock restarts on the next peripheral clock edge and any conversion under way is dropped. The bit stays set until the flush is done, then the ADC carries on, starting a new conversion if one was pending. A 0 does nothing.

values.text: Pipeline flushed, conversions under way lost.

fields.name: GAIN
fields.text: Gain of the ADC gain stage: 0x0 1x, 0x1 2x, 0x2 4x, 0x3 8x, 0x4 16x, 0xF 1/2x; 0x5 to 0xE reserved.

fields.name: INPUTOFFSET
fields.text: Offset added to MUXPOS during a pin scan (on when INPUTSCAN is not 0): each conversion uses input MUXPOS + INPUTOFFSET, and INPUTOFFSET goes up by one after every conversion.

fields.name: INPUTSCAN
fields.text: Number of inputs in a pin scan, minus one: the scan covers MUXPOS + INPUTOFFSET through MUXPOS + INPUTOFFSET + INPUTSCAN, and must stay within the inputs the device has.

fields.name: MUXNEG
fields.text: Picks the negative ADC input.

fields.name: MUXPOS
fields.text: Picks the positive ADC input; choosing the bandgap or the temperature sensor calls for a matching SAMPCTRL.SAMPLEN.

fields.name: WINMONEO
fields.text: Lets the window monitor send an output event when its condition is met.

fields.name: RESRDYEO
fields.text: Lets the ADC send an output event when a result is ready.

fields.name: SYNCEI
fields.text: Makes any incoming event flush the ADC and start a new conversion.

values.text: Any event flushes and starts a conversion.

fields.name: STARTEI
fields.text: Makes any incoming event start a conversion.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: A 1 turns off the synchronization ready interrupt and its pending request; a 0 does nothing.

values.text: Interrupt on; requested when INTFLAG.SYNCRDY sets.

fields.name: WINMON
fields.text: A 1 turns off the window monitor interrupt and its pending request; a 0 does nothing.

values.text: Interrupt on; requested when INTFLAG.WINMON sets.

fields.name: OVERRUN
fields.text: A 1 turns off the overrun interrupt and its pending request; a 0 does nothing.

values.text: Interrupt on; requested when INTFLAG.OVERRUN sets.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: A 1 turns off the result ready interrupt and its pending request; a 0 does nothing.

values.text: Interrupt on; requested when INTFLAG.RESRDY sets.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: A 1 turns on the synchronization ready interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WINMON
fields.text: A 1 turns on the window monitor interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVERRUN
fields.text: A 1 turns on the overrun interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: A 1 turns on the result ready interrupt; a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Goes high when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless an enable or software reset caused it, and raises an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.SYNCRDY is 1. Writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WINMON
fields.text: Goes high one GCLK_ADC cycle after the window monitor condition matches, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.WINMON is 1. Cleared by writing 1 or by reading RESULT; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: OVERRUN
fields.text: Goes high when RESULT is overwritten before the CPU has read the previous value, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.OVERRUN is 1. Writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: RESRDY
fields.text: Goes high when a conversion result is ready, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.RESRDY is 1. Cleared by writing 1 or by reading RESULT; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: High while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; drops to 0 when that finishes.

fields.name: RESULT
fields.text: The conversion result, up to 16 bits. Single-ended without averaging gives 12 bits: in [11:0] when right-aligned, or with the top byte in [15:8] and the low 4 bits in [7:4] when CTRLB.LEFTADJ is set, so an 8-bit result can be read from the high byte alone. With oversampling the result fills [15:0] as AVGCTRL sets.

fields.name: WINLT
fields.text: Lower limit for the window monitor, used when it is on.

fields.name: WINUT
fields.text: Upper limit for the window monitor, used when it is on.

fields.name: GAINCORR
fields.text: Gain error correction applied to the result when CTRLB.CORREN is 1: a fixed-point number with 1 integer bit and 11 fraction bits, from 0.10000000000 to 1.11111111111 binary, so 1/2 <= GAINCORR < 2.

fields.name: OFFSETCORR
fields.text: Offset error correction applied to the result when CTRLB.CORREN is 1, as a two's complement number.

fields.name: BIAS_CAL
fields.text: Bias calibration from production test; software copies it unchanged from the NVM software calibration area to reach the rated accuracy.

fields.name: LINEARITY_CAL
fields.text: Linearity calibration from production test; software copies it unchanged from the NVM software calibration area to reach the rated accuracy.

fields.name: DBGRUN
fields.text: Keeps the ADC running while the CPU is halted in debug mode. Writable only with the ADC off, and only while no conversion is under way.

fields.name: LPMUX
fields.text: Trades input mux resistance for power at low supply voltage. Not synchronized.

values.text: Low-resistance muxes that use more power at low voltage, for example when the voltage doubler drives them.
High-resistance muxes that use less power at low voltage, for example with the voltage doubler off.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Chooses whether the comparators keep working in standby sleep mode. Not synchronized.

values.text: Comparator pair keeps running in sleep.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the AC on or off; the written value reads back at once and STATUS.SYNCBUSY stays set until the synchronized change is done.

values.text: AC on; each comparator still needs its own COMPCTRLn.ENABLE.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1 returns every AC register to its reset value and turns the AC off; it overrides any other write in the same access, and SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both drop to 0 once the synchronized reset is done. A 0 does nothing.

fields.name: STARTx
fields.text: A 1 starts one single-shot comparison on comparator x when its COMPCTRLx.SINGLE and COMPCTRLx.ENABLE are both 1; otherwise, or if comparator x does not exist, it does nothing. A 0 does nothing; always reads 0.

fields.name: COMPEIx
fields.text: Makes any incoming event start a comparison on comparator x. When several events are routed in, any of them triggers it and the source cannot be told apart.

fields.name: WINEO0
fields.text: Lets window 0 send a peripheral event.

fields.name: COMPEOx
fields.text: Lets the output of comparator x send a peripheral event.

fields.name: WIN0
fields.text: Reads back whether the window 0 interrupt is on; a 1 turns it off, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: COMPx
fields.text: Reads back whether the comparator x interrupt is on; a 1 turns it off, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WIN0
fields.text: Reads back whether the window 0 interrupt is on; a 1 turns it on, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: COMPx
fields.text: Reads back whether the comparator x interrupt is on; a 1 turns it on, a 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WIN0
fields.text: Goes high on the condition chosen by WINCTRL.WINTSEL0, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.WIN0 is 1. Writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: COMPx
fields.text: Comparator x interrupt flag; goes high on the condition chosen by COMPCTRLx.INTSEL, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.COMPx is 1, and reads 0 for a comparator that does not exist. Writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: WSTATE0
fields.text: Where the signal sits relative to window 0 when window 0 mode is on: 0x0 ABOVE, 0x1 INSIDE, 0x2 BELOW, 0x3 reserved. Reads 0 if window 0 does not exist.

fields.name: STATEx
fields.text: Present output level of comparator x; valid only while STATUSB.READYx is 1.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: High while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; drops to 0 when that finishes.

fields.name: READYx
fields.text: High when the output of comparator x is ready, low when it is not; reads 0 for a comparator that does not exist.

fields.name: WSTATE0
fields.text: Where the signal sits relative to window 0 when window 0 mode is on: 0x0 ABOVE, 0x1 INSIDE, 0x2 BELOW, 0x3 reserved. Reads 0 if window 0 does not exist.

fields.name: STATEx
fields.text: Present output level of comparator x; reads 0 for a comparator that does not exist and is valid only while STATUSB.READYx is 1.

fields.name: WINTSEL0
fields.text: Window 0 interrupt condition: 0x0 signal above the window, 0x1 inside, 0x2 below, 0x3 outside.

fields.name: WEN0
fields.text: Turns on window mode for comparators 0 and 1.

values.text: Window mode on for comparators 0 and 1.

fields.name: FLEN
fields.text: Output filter of comparator n: 0x0 none, 0x1 majority of 3, 0x2 majority of 5, 0x3 to 0x7 reserved. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

fields.name: HYST
fields.text: Hysteresis on comparator n, in continuous mode only (COMPCTRLn.SINGLE = 0). Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

fields.name: OUT
fields.text: What reaches the COMPn I/O pin: 0x0 nothing, 0x1 the asynchronous output, 0x2 the synchronous filtered output, 0x3 reserved. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

values.name: OFF
values.text: COMPn pin not driven by the comparator.

values.name: ASYNC
values.text: Asynchronous COMPn output on the COMPn pin.

values.name: SYNC
values.text: Synchronous, filtered COMPn output on the COMPn pin.

fields.name: SWAP
fields.text: Exchanges the positive and negative inputs of COMPn and inverts its output, usable for offset cancellation. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

values.text: MUXPOS to the positive input, MUXNEG to the negative input.
MUXNEG to the positive input, MUXPOS to the negative input.

fields.name: MUXPOS
fields.text: Positive input of comparator n: 0x0 to 0x3 I/O pins 0 to 3. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

fields.name: MUXNEG
fields.text: Negative input of comparator n. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

fields.name: INTSEL
fields.text: What makes comparator n raise its interrupt or event: 0x0 output toggles, 0x1 output rises, 0x2 output falls, 0x3 a comparison ends (single-shot only). Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

values.name: EOC
values.text: Interrupt when a comparison ends; single-shot mode only.

fields.name: SPEED
fields.text: Speed and propagation delay of comparator n: 0x0 low, 0x1 high, 0x2 and 0x3 reserved. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

fields.name: SINGLE
fields.text: Chooses single-shot or continuous operation for comparator n. Writable only while COMPCTRLn.ENABLE is 0; not synchronized.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns comparator n on (1) or off (0). After a write the bit keeps showing the old state until the change completes, at least two GCLK_AC_DIG cycles for synchronization. While it is 1 the other COMPCTRLn bits are locked, until a 0 has been written and synchronized.

fields.name: VALUE
fields.text: Scaling factor of channel n of the VDD scaler: VSCALE = VDD x (VALUE + 1) / 64.

fields.name: RUNSTDBY
fields.text: Chooses whether the DAC output buffer may stay on in standby sleep mode. Not synchronized.

values.text: Output buffer may stay on in standby.

fields.name: ENABLE
fields.text: Turns the DAC on or off; the written value reads back at once while STATUS.SYNCBUSY stays set until the synchronized change is done.

fields.name: SWRST
fields.text: A 1 returns every DAC register to its reset value and turns the DAC off; it overrides any other write in the same access, and SWRST and STATUS.SYNCBUSY both drop to 0 once the synchronized reset is done. A 0 does nothing.

fields.name: REFSEL
fields.text: DAC reference voltage: 0x0 INT1V internal 1.0 V, 0x1 AVCC, 0x2 VREFA external, 0x3 reserved.

fields.name: BDWP
fields.text: Lets DATABUF be written past the Peripheral Access Controller write protection.

fields.name: VPD
fields.text: Turns off the voltage pump.

values.text: Pump switched on and off automatically.

fields.name: LEFTADJ
fields.text: Alignment of the 10-bit value in DATA and DATABUF.

fields.name: IOEN
fields.text: Routes the DAC output internally to the AC.

values.text: Internal output on, for the AC.

fields.name: EOEN
fields.text: Drives the DAC output onto the VOUT pin.

fields.name: EMPTYEO
fields.text: Lets the DAC send an event when DATABUF becomes empty.

fields.name: STARTEI
fields.text: Makes an incoming event move DATABUF into DATA and start a conversion.

fields.name: SYNCRDY
fields.text: Goes high when STATUS.SYNCBUSY falls from 1 to 0, unless an enable or software reset caused it, and raises an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.READY is 1. Writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: EMPTY
fields.text: Goes high when DATABUF has moved into DATA and the DAC can take new data in DATABUF, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.EMPTY is 1. Cleared by writing 1 or by writing DATABUF; writing 0 does nothing.

fields.name: UNDERRUN
fields.text: Goes high when a start conversion event arrives with DATABUF empty, raising an interrupt if INTENCLR/SET.UNDERRUN is 1. Writing 1 clears it; 0 does nothing.

fields.name: SYNCBUSY
fields.text: High while registers are being synchronized between clock domains; drops to 0 when that finishes.

fields.name: DATA
fields.text: The 10-bit value the DAC turns into a voltage, held in DATA[9:0] when CTRLB.LEFTADJ is 0 and in DATA[15:6] when it is 1.

fields.name: DATABUF
fields.text: The 10-bit value waiting to be moved into DATA, held in DATABUF[9:0] when CTRLB.LEFTADJ is 0 and in DATABUF[15:6] when it is 1.
